the Gemara's own clarification of when the mishna's 'they brought the High Priest down' actually occurred, ruling out ordinary days (which don't require the High Priest specifically) and moonlit nights near month's end being mistaken for dawn (l24); Rashi's explanation that the Mishnah's 'brought out to the place of burning' and 'brought the High Priest down' are two separate matters, the second returning the narrative to its proper place in the Yom Kippur order (l27); and the beraita establishing that not only offerings slaughtered at night but also nighttime pinching of a bird-offering and taking a handful of a meal-offering must be burned, since both are derived from the same slaughtering-law category, with the immediate distinction drawn between an irreversible bird-offering ('what was, was') and a still-correctable handful of meal-offering (l28).
